entry.title: SBND first results
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Short-Baseline Near Detector at Fermilab released its first neutrino-argon cross-section measurement. It covers muon neutrino charged-current interactions with a single proton and no pions in the final state, as functions of transverse kinematic imbalance variables. The analysis used a subset of Run 1 data corresponding to 8.8×10^19 protons-on-target and selected 12,804 signal candidates with a purity of 91%. The authors state that the cross sections discriminate strongly among event-generator predictions. Fermilab describes the result as improving neutrino interaction modelling in preparation for DUNE.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab reports that construction of the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility is entering its next phase, with critical components arriving and partner institutions contributing. Separately, UK groups have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies they are producing for DUNE. These sensors detect the electrical signals produced when neutrinos interact in the liquid argon.

entry.title: KM3NeT and gravitational waves
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT published a paper describing a search for joint observations of high-energy neutrinos and gravitational waves, using KM3NeT and ANTARES data from the O3 observing run. The motivation given is that gravitational-wave sources may produce high-energy neutrinos. The news item does not give the outcome of the search. The collaboration also held its Autumn 2026 meeting in Siracusa, with status updates on detector operations on the agenda.

entry.title: KM3-230213A review
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new review summarises the properties of the ultra-high-energy event KM3-230213A, detected by KM3NeT with an inferred parent-neutrino energy of O(10^17 eV). It discusses interpretations involving active galactic nuclei, transient sources and cosmogenic neutrinos, and the role of multi-messenger constraints. According to the abstract, no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been found despite extensive follow-up observations.

entry.title: TAMBO prototype
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. TAMBO aims to detect tau neutrinos from 1 PeV to 1,000 PeV, an energy range between the reach of optical-Cherenkov and radio-based experiments. It will use up to 5,000 particle detectors installed on the face of a steep hill in the Colca valley. A proceedings contribution presents the project and the TAMBITO prototype.

entry.title: nEXO cosmogenic backgrounds
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The nEXO collaboration evaluated the expected cosmogenic background rate for its five-tonne liquid xenon time projection chamber at SNOLAB, its preferred host site. The study compares Geant4 and FLUKA simulations of muons reaching the underground site and the radioactive isotopes they produce. The work addresses background mitigation for the neutrinoless double beta decay search in xenon-136.

entry.title: Project 8 atom source
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Project 8 aims to measure the neutrino mass from tritium beta decay using cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy, with a final sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2. A new paper reports a prototype electron cyclotron resonance dissociator for hydrogen, using a tunable 1 kW, 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets to ignite a plasma. This is one stage of the planned atomic-tritium beamline.

entry.title: CMS heavy neutral leptons
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CMS posted two searches for heavy neutral leptons in 13 TeV proton-proton data. One targets a Majorana HNL in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavour dileptons, using 138 fb^-1. The other targets long-lived HNLs from W decays, with one prompt muon and a displaced vertex of two muons reconstructed in the muon system.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies the contribution of Δ-direct-Urca processes to neutrino emissivity in neutron stars, motivated by the possible presence of Δ isobars in dense cores. It matters for neutron-star cooling, where nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes have been the dominant mechanisms.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors investigate whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for cross-section and hadronic-interaction uncertainties.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: any completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is blind to a Majorana phase in two-flavour oscillations. It also identifies how a rate anisotropy in the decoherence can act as an environmental phase reference. This clarifies when open-system effects could reveal a Majorana phase.

entry.title: The authors use solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free U
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors use solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models with kinetic and mass mixing. They derive exclusion limits for six benchmark models and find that their stringency depends on the leptonic charge assignments.

entry.title: The paper studies thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where neutrino masses arise from
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model accommodates sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale, and the paper examines whether leptogenesis is viable in it.

entry.title: The authors compute the detectability of neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae through nuclear
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors compute the detectability of neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae through nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals. They include variations in neutron-star mass, failed supernovae forming black holes, and the nuclear equation of state, and quantify the sensitivity gain for models with larger neutrino emission.
